claims.claim: pytest collects one test per parametrize value; fixtures with yield run teardown after; scope='session' builds once per run.
claims.source: pytest 9.1.1 behaviour, used by this repository's own test suite.

concept_html:
pytest finds files named test_*.py, runs every function named test_*, and reports each failing assert with the values on both sides. No classes or special assert methods are needed.

def test_weighted_share_uses_weights() -> None:
    assert weighted_share([1, 0], [3.0, 1.0]) == 0.75

Fixtures provide what tests need. A test names a fixture as a parameter, and pytest builds it and passes it in. For Spark, one fixture creates the session:

@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def spark() -> Iterator[SparkSession]:
    session = SparkSession.builder.master("local[2]").getOrCreate()
    yield session
    session.stop()
  • scope="session" builds it once for the whole test run. Starting Spark takes several seconds. Once per test, and a 40-test suite spends minutes on start-up alone.
  • yield hands the value to the tests. The code after yield runs once at the end, which is where you stop the session.
  • Put shared fixtures in conftest.py. pytest loads it automatically for every test in that folder and below.

@pytest.mark.parametrize runs one test with several inputs, and each input is reported as its own test:

@pytest.mark.parametrize(("flags", "weights", "expected"), [([1], [2.0], 1.0), ([0, 0], [1.0, 1.0], 0.0)])
def test_share(flags, weights, expected): ...

A good test fails for the bug you fear. Write it against the known answer on small data, including the edge cases: empty input, zero totals, missing values. Check it by breaking the code on purpose and watching the test fail.

lines: from collections.abc import Iterator
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def spark() -> Iterator[SparkSession]:
"""One local session for the whole test run."""
session = SparkSession.builder.master("local[2]").config("spark.ui.enabled", "false").getOrCreate()
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
("flags", "weights", "expected"),
([1, 0, 1], [2.0, 1.0, 1.0], 0.75),
([0, 0], [1.0, 1.0], 0.0),
([1, 0], [0.0, 0.0], None),
def test_weighted_share(flags: list[int], weights: list[float], expected: float | None) -> None:
assert weighted_share(flags, weights) == expected

title: pytest basics, and a SparkSession fixture shared by every test
why_html:
A team's test for weighted_share checks that the result is between 0 and 1. The function is later rewritten and accidentally returns the unweighted share. The result is still between 0 and 1, so the test passes, and weighted reach in the dashboard is wrong for a month.

A test with a known answer, weighted_share([1, 0], [3.0, 1.0]) == 0.75, fails the moment the weights are ignored, because the unweighted answer is 0.5.
